Заклёпка.sourceClaims: RP p.30 explicitly treats rivets as permanent fasteners and drilling as removal. The Russian usually is weaker than the manual categorical wording and does not claim drilling is the only conceivable operation.
Заклёпка.usefulness: Adds the practical cost of dismantling: drilling out the fastener; this is absent from the head-forming question and is more than a reworded definition.
Заклёпка.grammar: Complete natural two-clause Russian sentence; крепёж refers to the rivet being removed.

sources.context: Rivets: permanent installation and drilling removal; Solid rivets shop head, Table IX including reference 21 and Briles footnote 13.

Болт.sourceClaims: RP p.5 explicitly says most bolts are carbon, alloy or stainless steel. Большинство preserves the qualifier and allows titanium/aluminium exceptions; the card makes no unsupported strength/corrosion claim.
Болт.usefulness: Adds material selection information rather than repeating the question or an external-thread definition.
Болт.grammar: Three parallel material adjectives share стали; изготавливают из is idiomatic.

sources.context: Fastener Materials, first paragraph; page read through Cadmium Plating and numbered precautions.

Гайка.sourceClaims: RP p.11 Nylok paragraph and fig.4 support projection, mating-thread compression and locking contact. This is a statement about a named nylon insert, not an assertion that every nut contains it. Nut-card explanation explicitly says Некоторые гайки; rivet-card note likewise has no universal quantifier. More explicit subtype wording would improve standalone clarity but the actual sentence does not claim all nuts have nylon.
Гайка.usefulness: Explains how one locking element works, beyond the internal-thread definition; a player learns a real mechanical effect.
Гайка.grammar: Two technical but complete clauses; сопряжённая резьба сжимает его clearly refers to the insert. No grammatical implication of universal possession.

sources.context: Nylok pellet paragraph and figure 4; contrasted with deformed-thread fig.3, collar fig.5, castellated fig.6 and Nylok footnote 8.

Винт.sourceClaims: FAQ p.383 explicitly rejects a universally acceptable distinction and concludes with geometry or corresponding part number. NASA is the publishing organisation; the card accurately attributes its advice without turning a local distinction into an absolute rule.
Винт.usefulness: Warns why a label alone is insufficient for selecting a part and names two practical alternatives. It does not simply repeat the screw definition.
Винт.grammar: Граница ... не универсальна is a comprehensible concise paraphrase; parallel geometry/part-number complement is clear.

sources.context: Q10/A10 entire page: four proposed bolt/screw distinctions, none universally acceptable, final instruction to specify geometry or part number.

pageContextRemarks: RP p.5 was read including limitations, numbered precautions and cadmium discussion; none is silently extended to every bolt.
RP p.11 figures distinguish multiple locknut types; Nylok is not treated as generic anatomy of all nuts. Footnote 8 is a trade-name attribution, not another mechanism.
RP p.30 table IX and footnote 13 were read; neither changes the permanent/drilling statements.
RP p.31 includes multiple blind-rivet mechanisms and tubular rivets; the question describes a valid formed-head type, not all installation methods.
FAQ p.383 was read in full including all four proposed definitions and concluding qualification; the claim is appropriately non-universal.
